title: Maloney et al. (2022), Surgical amputation of a limb 31,000 years ago in Borneo
use: Liang Tebo burial, missing lower left limb, healing, research estimate of survival, proposed deliberate amputation. State interpretation as attributed and include the published challenge.

title: Murphy et al. (2023), Common orthopaedic trauma may explain 31,000-year-old remains
use: Published alternative explanation involving severe fracture during growth. Do not claim the original paper was retracted or that the alternative was established.

title: Vlok et al. (2023), Reply to: Common orthopaedic trauma may explain 31,000-year-old remains
use: Original team's rebuttal based on injury location and morphology; continued defense of amputation interpretation.

title: Smithsonian Human Origins Program — Shanidar 1
use: Injury and healing, impaired right arm, possible left-eye injury, healed right-foot fracture, age-at-death estimate around 35–45, inferred social support.

title: The Shanidar Cave Project — Previous excavations
use: Geographic setting, archaeological context, care as interpretation. Avoid resolving differing published chronological estimates with a single precise date.

title: Spikins et al. — Living to fight another day: The ecological and evolutionary significance of Neanderthal healthcare
use: Research argument for care as a contribution to survival. Attribute as a research interpretation, not a universal prehistoric behavior.

title: NHS — Broken leg
use: Modern comparison: usual healing range 6–12 weeks, sometimes longer; differing injury severity. Never apply the modern timeline as a measured Stone Age recovery rate.

title: Health New Zealand — Broken lower leg (fractured tibia or fibula)
use: General complications including infection with broken skin and pressure on nearby nerves and blood vessels. Historical explainer only; no treatment instructions.
